notes.md: - **Kshetrayya:** Telugu composer of **padams** (sringara songs), linked with **Movva (Muvva)**, Krishna district; signature (mudra) **Muvva Gopala**. Patron: **Vijayaraghava Nayaka**, the **last Nayaka king of Tanjore**.

new.s: To the reign of which Vijayanagara ruler does the Vilapakam inscription of 1601 belong?
new.x: The Vilapakam inscription (1601), giving the Tuluva and Aravidu genealogy, belongs to Venkatapati Raya II.
new.angle: U0127 notes gap: Vilapakam inscription -> Venkatapati II

new.s: At whose court did Appayya Dikshita, author of Shaivarka Mani Dipika, live?
new.x: Appayya Dikshita was a scholar at the court of Venkatapati Raya II.
new.angle: U0127 notes gap: Appayya Dikshita -> court of Venkatapati II

new.s: From which place did the Damarla Nayaks, who granted the site of Madras, rule?
new.x: The Damarla Nayaks, Velama feudatories of the Aravidus, ruled from Srikalahasti.
new.angle: U0127 notes gap: Damarla Nayaks -> Srikalahasti

new.s: Who is the author of 'A Forgotten Empire' (1900) on Vijayanagara?
new.x: Robert Sewell wrote A Forgotten Empire in 1900.
new.angle: U0127 notes gap: A Forgotten Empire -> Sewell

new.s: Aliya Rama Raya, the regent at the time of Talikota, was the son-in-law of which ruler?
new.x: Aliya ('son-in-law') Rama Raya was the son-in-law of Krishnadevaraya.
new.angle: U0127 notes gap: Rama Raya -> son-in-law of Krishnadevaraya

new.s: The Mughals were Chagatai Turks. After whom was the Chagatai line named?
o: The second son of Chingiz Khan
The founder of the Uzbek khanate
new.x: Chagatai was Genghis (Chingiz) Khan's second son, ruler of Central Asia and Turkistan.
new.angle: U0128 notes gap: Chagatai Turks -> second son of Chingiz Khan

new.s: What does the name 'Babur' mean?
new.x: Babur, the nickname of Zahir-ud-din Muhammad, means tiger.
new.angle: U0128 notes gap: Babur -> tiger

new.s: What was the original name of Sher Shah Suri?
new.x: Sher Shah was born Farid (Farid Khan); Jalal Khan was his son Islam Shah.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Sher Shah -> original name Farid

new.s: Sher Shah's father was an Afghan jagirdar of which place?
new.x: Farid was the son of an Afghan jagirdar of Sasaram, of the Sur tribe.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Sher Shah -> father's jagir Sasaram

new.s: Which city, where young Farid (Sher Shah) studied, was called 'Siraj-i-Hind'?
new.x: Farid studied at Jaunpur, known as Siraj-i-Hind.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Jaunpur -> Siraj-i-Hind

new.s: Who among the following was the mother of Akbar?
new.x: Humayun married Hamida Banu Begum, Akbar's mother; Akbar was born at Amarkot in 1542.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Hamida Banu -> Akbar's mother

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a brother of Humayun?
new.x: Kamran, Askari and Hindal were Humayun's rival brothers; Mirza Hakim was Akbar's half-brother.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Humayun's brothers

new.s: In Sher Shah's army, what did 'chehra' (huliya) mean?
new.x: Chehra or huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers; dagh was horse branding. Both checked fraud.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Sur army -> chehra

new.s: In a Sur-era pargana, who were the Karkuns?
o: Writers keeping records in Hindi and Persian
new.x: Karkuns were writers who kept records in Hindi and Persian.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Sur pargana -> karkuns

new.s: Under Sher Shah, what was the 'muhasilana'?
o: The fee paid to the revenue collector
The fee paid to the surveyor
The title deed given to the cultivator
The deed of acceptance signed by the peasant
new.x: Muhasilana was the collector's fee; jaribana was the surveyor's fee.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Sher Shah revenue -> muhasilana

new.s: Who completed Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram?
new.x: Sher Shah began his octagonal tomb at Sasaram; his son Islam Shah completed it.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Sher Shah's tomb -> completed by Islam Shah

new.s: Under whose supervision was the Rohtas Fort near Jhelum begun by Sher Shah in 1541?
new.x: Rohtas Fort was begun in 1541 under Todar Mal, who later served Akbar.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Rohtas Fort -> Todar Mal

new.s: Who built the tomb of Sikandar Lodi in Delhi?
new.x: Sikandar Lodi's tomb in Delhi was built by his son Ibrahim Lodi.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Sikandar Lodi's tomb -> Ibrahim Lodi

new.s: In which year was Humayun's Tomb in Delhi declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
new.x: Humayun's Tomb became a UNESCO site in 1993; Rohtas Fort followed in 1997.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Humayun's Tomb -> UNESCO 1993

new.s: In which year was Sher Shah's Rohtas Fort inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
new.x: Rohtas Fort near Jhelum, Pakistan, became a UNESCO site in 1997.
new.angle: U0129 notes gap: Rohtas Fort -> UNESCO 1997

new.s: From whom did Akbar conquer Malwa in 1561?
new.x: Malwa was taken in 1561 from the Afghan ruler Baz Bahadur.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Malwa -> Baz Bahadur

new.s: Who was the ruler of Mewar when Akbar captured Chittor in 1568?
new.x: Chittor fell in 1568 during the rule of Rana Udai Singh.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Chittor -> Udai Singh

new.s: In which year did Akbar capture Chittor?
new.x: Akbar took Chittor in 1568 and Ranthambore in 1569.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Chittor -> 1568

new.s: Who was the Afghan ruler of Bengal whom Akbar's forces defeated in 1576?
new.x: Bengal (with Bihar) was conquered in 1576 from Daud Khan Karrani, son of Sulaiman.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Bengal -> Daud Khan Karrani

new.s: Against whom did Akbar march to Kabul in 1581?
new.x: In 1581 Akbar marched on Kabul against his half-brother Mirza Hakim.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Kabul -> Mirza Hakim

new.s: In which year was Akbar's Ibadat Khana opened to Hindus, Jains, Christians and Zoroastrians?
new.x: Built in 1575 for Muslim divines, the Ibadat Khana was opened to all faiths in 1578.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Ibadat Khana -> opened to all 1578

new.s: Akbar issued coins with figures of Rama and Sita bearing which Devanagari legend?
new.x: Akbar's Rama-Sita coins carry the Devanagari legend 'Rama-Siya'.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Akbar coins -> Rama-Siya

new.s: Which Mughal emperor ended the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad at the request of Kavindracharya?
new.x: Shah Jahan ended the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad after Kavindracharya and the Banaras pandits asked.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Pilgrim tax Banaras -> Shah Jahan

new.s: Which Mughal emperor abolished sijda (prostration before the emperor)?
new.x: Sijda, begun by Balban, was ended by Shah Jahan.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Sijda -> ended by Shah Jahan

new.s: In medieval Islamic taxation, what was 'Haqq-e-Sharb'?
new.x: Haqq-e-Sharb was the irrigation tax; zakat was alms tax and ushr land tax on Muslims.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Haqq-e-Sharb -> irrigation tax

new.s: Which Mughal emperor banned the celebration of Navroz?
new.x: Aurangzeb, who also reimposed jizya in 1679, banned Navroz.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Aurangzeb -> banned Navroz

new.s: Who among the following called Din-i-Ilahi a religion in his Dabistan-i-Mazahib?
new.x: Mohsin Fani, a contemporary of Jahangir, called it a religion in the Dabistan-i-Mazahib.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Din-i-Ilahi -> Mohsin Fani

new.s: Who founded the Qadiri Sufi order?
new.x: The Qadiri order was founded by Abdul Qadir Jilani; Dara Shikoh followed it.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Qadiri -> Abdul Qadir Jilani

new.s: Who brought the Suhrawardi Sufi order to Multan?
new.x: The Suhrawardi order of Shahabuddin was brought to Multan by Bahauddin Zakariya.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Suhrawardi -> Bahauddin Zakariya, Multan

new.s: Who translated the Lilavati into Persian in Akbar's time?
new.x: Faizi, Akbar's poet laureate and Abul Fazl's brother, made the Persian Lilavati.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Lilavati -> Faizi

new.s: Under what name did Abul Fazl render the Panchatantra into Persian?
new.x: Abul Fazl's Persian Panchatantra is the Ayar-i-Danish.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Panchatantra -> Ayar-i-Danish

new.s: Who was the father of Abul Fazl and Faizi?
new.x: Sheikh Mubarak, who drafted the Mahzar, was the father of Abul Fazl and Faizi.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Abul Fazl, Faizi -> father Sheikh Mubarak

new.s: Which title did Akbar confer on Tansen?
new.x: Akbar gave Tansen the title 'Miyan' (hence Miyan ki Malhar); the name Tansen came from an earlier Hindu patron.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Tansen -> title Miyan

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Land assignment – Rulers) is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: Mokasa was the Maratha assignment; the Mughals used jagirs.
new.angle: U0130 notes gap: Land grants -> dynasty

new.s: Under Akbar's Zabti system, what were the 'dasturs'?
o: Cash revenue rates per crop per bigha
Revenue circles yielding one crore dams
new.x: Under zabti, land was measured and dasturs fixed cash rates per crop per bigha.
new.angle: U0131 notes gap: Zabti -> dasturs

new.s: In parts of the Deccan, on what basis was land revenue fixed under the plough method?
o: An estimate of the standing crop
new.x: In parts of the Deccan revenue was assessed by the number of ploughs.
new.angle: U0131 notes gap: Plough assessment -> Deccan

new.s: What was the range of mansab ranks for nobles under Akbar?
new.x: Nobles held mansabs from 10 to 5,000 (later 7,000); higher ranks went only to princes.
new.angle: U0131 notes gap: Mansab -> range of ranks

new.s: Which Mughal central minister looked after the royal household and the karkhanas?
new.x: The Mir Saman was in charge of the royal household and karkhanas.
new.angle: U0131 notes gap: Mir Saman -> household

new.s: To which Persian ruler did Jahangir lose Kandahar in 1622?
new.x: Kandahar was lost to Shah Abbas I of Persia in 1622.
new.angle: U0132 notes gap: Kandahar 1622 -> Shah Abbas I

new.s: Which English captain defeated the Portuguese off Surat in 1612, leading to the English factory at Surat?
new.x: Captain Best beat the Portuguese off Surat in 1612; the Surat factory followed in 1613.
new.angle: U0132 notes gap: Captain Best -> Surat 1612

new.s: Which European traveller described the Peacock Throne of Shah Jahan?
new.x: The French jeweller Tavernier described the Peacock Throne.
new.angle: U0132 notes gap: Peacock Throne -> Tavernier

new.s: Who drove the English under Job Charnock out of Hooghly in 1686?
new.x: In the first Mughal-British conflict (1686), Shaista Khan drove the English out of Hooghly.
new.angle: U0132 notes gap: 1686 Hooghly -> Shaista Khan

new.s: Which Bundela chief revolted early in Shah Jahan's reign?
new.x: Shah Jahan's early revolts were by the Bundela Jujhar Singh and Khan Jahan Lodi.
new.angle: U0132 notes gap: Shah Jahan early revolts -> Jujhar Singh

new.s: In which year did Aurangzeb annex Golconda?
new.x: Golconda was annexed in 1687 as the 21st suba; Bijapur fell in 1686.
new.angle: U0132 notes gap: Golconda annexed -> 1687

new.s: Whom did Aurangzeb and Murad defeat in the Battle of Dharmat (1658)?
new.x: At Dharmat near Ujjain, Aurangzeb and Murad beat Jaswant Singh, who led Dara's army.
new.angle: U0132 notes gap: Dharmat -> Jaswant Singh

new.s: Who defeated Shah Shuja at Bahadurgarh near Banaras in 1658?
new.x: Dara's son Sulaiman Shikoh defeated Shuja at Bahadurgarh in February 1658.
new.angle: U0132 notes gap: Bahadurgarh -> Sulaiman Shikoh

new.s: Which title did Nur Jahan later receive?
new.x: Mehrunnisa was titled Nur Jahan and later Padshah Begum; Sahibat-uz-Zamani was Jahanara's title.
new.angle: U0132 notes gap: Nur Jahan -> Padshah Begum

new.s: Kshetrayya, the Telugu padam composer linked with Movva in Krishna district, used which name of the deity as his signature (mudra)?
new.x: Kshetrayya signed his padams with Muvva Gopala, Krishna of Muvva (Movva).
new.angle: U0127 web: PYQ yf03eb99786c Kshetrayya -> Tanjore Nayaka patron: Kshetrayya -> mudra Muvva Gopala

new.s: Who was the last Nayaka king of Tanjore, at whose court Kshetrayya composed padams?
new.x: Vijayaraghava Nayaka, the last Nayaka king of Tanjore, was a patron of Kshetrayya.
new.angle: U0127 web: PYQ yf03eb99786c Kshetrayya -> Tanjore Nayaka patron: Kshetrayya -> patron, last Tanjore Nayaka
